rationale: Dawn already reported uncaptured errors and device loss through its own callbacks, but those messages only reached runtime::log_error, so a validation error that dropped a frame never appeared on the timeline beside the frame it killed. A gpu trace category already existed and nothing emitted into it from these paths. The change adds instant-event macros to Pulp's trace API and a shared sink that the Dawn callbacks feed, keeping their existing log_error calls so no current behaviour regresses; the event name stays an interned StaticString with the message as a debug annotation because these callbacks run on the render thread. The touched Dawn file gains only the emit calls, and the iOS-Simulator warning filter is preserved byte-identical and still precedes them. This wires a transferred-slice callback into Pulp's own runtime tracing, which is Pulp host-integration work with no named immutable Vellum framework commit to backport, so it is dispositioned pulp-only.
tests: an installed Skia handler forwards records into the same sink
emit_gpu_diagnostic counts every record it is handed
